html:
SMTO-HTTP-0054 — The Gateway sent back a reply SMTO couldn't read

GUID: 2809fd0c-a4be-4b95-b1ac-4c5705aeb6ab
Slug: http-gateway-invalid-response
Domain: HTTP · Subsystem: http

What happened

  • The Gateway answered the web request, but its reply was incomplete or in a form SMTO doesn't accept, so SMTO couldn't use the result. This usually means SMTO and the Gateway are on different versions.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways, select Check for updates and install any update offered for the Gateway this task used. A reply SMTO can't read usually comes from a Gateway that is older or newer than SMTO.
  2. If the request was signing in to a service that asks you to approve access in your browser, start a new task after the update and approve the sign-in when SMTO asks. The approval prompt was missing from the Gateway's reply, so SMTO couldn't show it to you.
  3. Before asking the Agent to repeat a request that changes something, open that service and check whether the change already happened. The Gateway may have completed the request even though SMTO couldn't read the reply.

What success looks like

  • After the update, the Agent's web request shows a normal result, or the sign-in approval appears.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO and its Gateways. Don't turn off security checks or remove saved data to make the reply go through.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway's http.request receipt failed the Server's result validation, or an http_oauth_authorization_required result arrived without its private authorization descriptor (_auth_ui).

What this means

  • A returned connection/resource receipt fails its schema, or an OAuth authorization-required response lacks its private UI descriptor. The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.

Why this can happen

  • A returned connection/resource receipt fails its schema, or an OAuth authorization-required response lacks its private UI descriptor.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect safe schema/descriptor diagnostics and build compatibility without treating an invalid receipt as no execution.

How to fix it

  • Compare the Server and Gateway versions and update the Gateway to the matching build (Settings › Setup › Gateways › Check for updates); read the Server log for the receipt validation diagnostic. For OAuth, confirm the Gateway build returns the authorization descriptor. Inspect the target's state before repeating any request that may have reached it.
  • Inspect the safe receipt validation diagnostic and verify controller/Gateway version compatibility. Restore the matching supported HTTP protocol; inspect remote state before repeating a request that may have reached its target.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The Gateway returns a valid accepted receipt, with prior possible effects reconciled separately.

What not to do

  • Do not remove retained state or weaken trust checks to make an unavailable dependency appear healthy.

Technical notes

  • The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
